claims.title: Tikal settled in the Peten
claims.summary: A village forms at Tikal in the Middle Formative period and grows into a ceremonial centre of the lowland Maya.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Guatemala: From the heartland of Classic Maya civilisation through Spanish conquest and a long, painful path to peace.", terralore.co/country/GTM/chronicle#ev-900bce-tikal-settled-in-the-peten, claim TL:GTM:event:900bce:tikal-settled-in-the-peten, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Tikal at its height
claims.summary: Tikal reaches its architectural and artistic peak as one of the dominant city-states of the Classic Maya world.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Guatemala: From the heartland of Classic Maya civilisation through Spanish conquest and a long, painful path to peace.", terralore.co/country/GTM/chronicle#ev-600-tikal-at-its-height, claim TL:GTM:event:600:tikal-at-its-height, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Classic Maya collapse
claims.summary: Tikal and the southern lowland centres are depopulated and abandoned as the Classic Maya order disintegrates.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Guatemala: From the heartland of Classic Maya civilisation through Spanish conquest and a long, painful path to peace.", terralore.co/country/GTM/chronicle#ev-900-classic-maya-collapse, claim TL:GTM:event:900:classic-maya-collapse, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Conquest under Pedro de Alvarado
claims.summary: Alvarado invades from Mexico, defeats the K'iche', and burns their capital Q'umarkaj, beginning Spanish rule in Guatemala.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Guatemala: From the heartland of Classic Maya civilisation through Spanish conquest and a long, painful path to peace.", terralore.co/country/GTM/chronicle#ev-1524-conquest-under-pedro-de-alvarado, claim TL:GTM:event:1524:conquest-under-pedro-de-alvarado, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Santiago de los Caballeros re-founded
claims.summary: After a flood destroys the earlier capital, the colonial seat of the Captaincy General is established at present-day Antigua Guatemala.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Guatemala: From the heartland of Classic Maya civilisation through Spanish conquest and a long, painful path to peace.", terralore.co/country/GTM/chronicle#ev-1543-santiago-de-los-caballeros-re-founded, claim TL:GTM:event:1543:santiago-de-los-caballeros-re-founded, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Popol Vuh set down
claims.summary: The K'iche' creation epic, the Popol Vuh, is written in alphabetic K'iche', preserving Maya mythology and dynastic history.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Guatemala: From the heartland of Classic Maya civilisation through Spanish conquest and a long, painful path to peace.", terralore.co/country/GTM/chronicle#ev-1554-the-popol-vuh-set-down, claim TL:GTM:event:1554:the-popol-vuh-set-down, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Santa Marta earthquakes ruin Antigua
claims.summary: Powerful earthquakes devastate the colonial capital, leading to the transfer of government to present-day Guatemala City.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Guatemala: From the heartland of Classic Maya civilisation through Spanish conquest and a long, painful path to peace.", terralore.co/country/GTM/chronicle#ev-1773-santa-marta-earthquakes-ruin-antigua, claim TL:GTM:event:1773:santa-marta-earthquakes-ruin-antigua, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Independence from Spain
claims.summary: Guatemala City signs the Act of Independence of Central America, ending nearly three centuries of Spanish rule.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Guatemala: From the heartland of Classic Maya civilisation through Spanish conquest and a long, painful path to peace.", terralore.co/country/GTM/chronicle#ev-1821-independence-from-spain, claim TL:GTM:event:1821:independence-from-spain, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Federal Republic of Central America
claims.summary: The former captaincy general forms a federation of five states, with Guatemala City as its capital.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Guatemala: From the heartland of Classic Maya civilisation through Spanish conquest and a long, painful path to peace.", terralore.co/country/GTM/chronicle#ev-1823-federal-republic-of-central-america, claim TL:GTM:event:1823:federal-republic-of-central-america, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Republic of Guatemala proclaimed
claims.summary: With the federation dissolved, Guatemala declares itself a sovereign republic under Conservative rule.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Guatemala: From the heartland of Classic Maya civilisation through Spanish conquest and a long, painful path to peace.", terralore.co/country/GTM/chronicle#ev-1847-republic-of-guatemala-proclaimed, claim TL:GTM:event:1847:republic-of-guatemala-proclaimed, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Liberal revolution
claims.summary: Justo Rufino Barrios and the Liberals seize power, launching coffee-based modernisation and the expropriation of communal and Maya lands.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Guatemala: From the heartland of Classic Maya civilisation through Spanish conquest and a long, painful path to peace.", terralore.co/country/GTM/chronicle#ev-1871-liberal-revolution, claim TL:GTM:event:1871:liberal-revolution, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The coffee economy
claims.summary: Coffee becomes Guatemala's dominant export, financing railways and ports while binding the Maya to plantation labour.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Guatemala: From the heartland of Classic Maya civilisation through Spanish conquest and a long, painful path to peace.", terralore.co/country/GTM/chronicle#ev-1873-the-coffee-economy, claim TL:GTM:event:1873:the-coffee-economy, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Rise of the United Fruit Company
claims.summary: United Fruit acquires extensive lands, railways, and the main port, becoming Guatemala's largest landowner and a dominant economic force.

sources.label: Foreign Relations of the United States, 1952-1954, Guatemala
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.title: Dictatorship of Jorge Ubico
claims.summary: General Ubico rules for thirteen years, repressing labour and opposition while sustaining the coffee oligarchy and ties to United Fruit.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Guatemala: From the heartland of Classic Maya civilisation through Spanish conquest and a long, painful path to peace.", terralore.co/country/GTM/chronicle#ev-1931-dictatorship-of-jorge-ubico, claim TL:GTM:event:1931:dictatorship-of-jorge-ubico, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: October Revolution
claims.summary: A popular uprising ends the Ubico dictatorship and ushers in democratic reform under Juan Jose Arevalo.

sources.label: Foreign Relations of the United States, 1952-1954, Guatemala
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Guatemala: From the heartland of Classic Maya civilisation through Spanish conquest and a long, painful path to peace.", terralore.co/country/GTM/chronicle#ev-1944-october-revolution, claim TL:GTM:event:1944:october-revolution, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Agrarian reform under Arbenz
claims.summary: President Arbenz's Decree 900 expropriates idle lands, including United Fruit estates, for the landless, alarming Washington.

sources.label: Foreign Relations of the United States, 1952-1954, Guatemala
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.title: CIA-backed coup overthrows Arbenz
claims.summary: The covert operation PBSUCCESS pressures Arbenz to resign on 27 June 1954, ending the reform era and installing military rule.

sources.label: Foreign Relations of the United States, 1952-1954, Guatemala
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.title: Civil war and the Maya genocide
claims.summary: A thirty-six-year conflict leaves some 200,000 dead or disappeared, mostly Maya, with the state held by the CEH to have committed genocide.

sources.label: Guatemala Peace Agreements, 1996 (Memory of the World)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Guatemala: From the heartland of Classic Maya civilisation through Spanish conquest and a long, painful path to peace.", terralore.co/country/GTM/chronicle#ev-1960-civil-war-and-the-maya-genocide, claim TL:GTM:event:1960:civil-war-and-the-maya-genocide, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Firm and Lasting Peace accords
claims.summary: The government and the URNG sign the final peace agreement in Guatemala City, ending the civil war.

sources.label: Guatemala Peace Agreements, 1996 (Memory of the World)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Guatemala: From the heartland of Classic Maya civilisation through Spanish conquest and a long, painful path to peace.", terralore.co/country/GTM/chronicle#ev-1996-firm-and-lasting-peace-accords, claim TL:GTM:event:1996:firm-and-lasting-peace-accords, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Memory of Silence report
claims.summary: The UN-backed Commission for Historical Clarification publishes its findings, attributing the bulk of wartime atrocities to the state and finding acts of genocide against the Maya.

sources.label: Guatemala Peace Agreements, 1996 (Memory of the World)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Guatemala: From the heartland of Classic Maya civilisation through Spanish conquest and a long, painful path to peace.", terralore.co/country/GTM/chronicle#ev-1999-memory-of-silence-report, claim TL:GTM:event:1999:memory-of-silence-report, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Rios Montt convicted of genocide
claims.summary: A Guatemalan court convicts the former dictator of genocide against the Ixil Maya, the first such verdict by a national court, though it is soon annulled.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Guatemala: From the heartland of Classic Maya civilisation through Spanish conquest and a long, painful path to peace.", terralore.co/country/GTM/chronicle#ev-2013-rios-montt-convicted-of-genocide, claim TL:GTM:event:2013:rios-montt-convicted-of-genocide, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Election of Bernardo Arevalo
claims.summary: Anti-corruption candidate Bernardo Arevalo wins the presidency and, despite attempts to block him, is inaugurated in January 2024.

sources.label: Sometimes the Good Guys Win: Guatemala's Shocking 2023 Election
